newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big trades in spotty session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big trades in spotty session.

text.p: Two equity options traded in very heavy volume Monday in a session marked by scattered options activity, traders said.

On the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, 8,500 of the CUC International Inc January 30 calls traded, including a block of 3,000 contracts at 7/16. The option's open interest was about 9,100 through last Friday.
The PHLX has two CUC options series because of a three-for-two stock split that took effect in October. CUC shares ended up 1-5/8 at 26-1/4 on consolidated volume of about 3.65 million shares.
On the Pacific Stock Exchange, 8,352 of the WorldCom Inc December 20 calls traded. Three sizable blocks crossed, one of 4,000 contracts and two of 2,000 each.
The option, which closed at 3-5/8, had open interest of 11,615. WorldCom shares finished at 23-3/8, down 3/8.
In other activity, the Philip Morris Cos Inc January 100 call was the most active option on the American Stock Exchange, with 3,253 contracts changing hands.
The option surged 2-1/4 to 6-7/8 as the shares rose also.

Philip Morris gained 3-1/4 to 105-1/2 in heavy trading. Dealers pegged the rally to news that U.S. Food and Drug Administration chief David Kessler, a vocal anti-smoking advocate, intends to leave his post.
The news also drove other tobacco shares higher.
Other busy Philip Morris options included the December 100 and 110 calls and the January 105 and 110 calls.
Two options on low-priced stocks also were active, Arakis Energy Corp and Echo Bay Mines Ltd.
On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Arakis January five call traded 3,776 contracts.
The Arakis Janury 7-1/2 call traded more than 1,600 contracts and the July 7-1/2 put traded 1,200.
A trader at the CBOE said investors were buying the calls at the 5 strikes and selling 7-1/2s and 10s.
Arakis shares ended up 17/32 at 6-9/32 on nearly four million shares.
Traders said investors were expecting news on the Canadian-based oil company's joint venture in Sudan before year-end.
For Echo Bay Mines, the April five call traded 7,880 contracts, mostly in a block of 6,750.
The option, which had open interest of five, fell 3/8 to 1-3/4. Echo Bay's shares fell 9/16 to 6-3/16 in U.S. trading.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said investors could be better served by buying low priced stocks outright rather than the options.

"Unfortunately, there's too much speculation going on in options on low-priced stocks in my opinion," he said. "People should be looking at buying the stocks as perpetual options. Why deal with an expiration?"
--Gregory Crawford, 312 408 8750
